question: Which islands of India are strategically important due to their location near the Malacca Strait? (RRB NTPC (UG) CBT-I (21/08/2025) Shift 2)
options: Gulf of Kutch Islands
Andaman and Nicobar Islands
Lakshadweep Islands
Rameswaram Islands
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Andaman and Nicobar Islands

Explanation:
The Andaman and Nicobar Islands are located in the Bay of Bengal and are strategically significant due to their proximity to the Malacca Strait. This strait connects the Indian Ocean to the Pacific Ocean, making it a crucial global trade route. For India, these islands are vital for maritime security and strategic surveillance. The Indian Navy maintains a base here, strengthening India's presence in the Indo-Pacific region. The islands also serve as a key point for monitoring sea lanes and projecting power in the region.

question: Acid rain is mainly caused due to the presence of which two gases in the atmosphere?  (RRB NTPC (UG) CBT-I (21/08/2025) Shift 2)
options: Oxygen and Hydrogen
Carbon dioxide and Carbon monoxide
Nitrogen and Methane
Sulphur dioxide and Nitrogen oxides
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Sulphur dioxide and Nitrogen oxides

Explanation:
Acid rain is primarily caused by the presence of sulphur dioxide (SO₂) and nitrogen oxides (NOₓ) in the atmosphere. These gases are mainly released from the combustion of fossil fuels (coal, petroleum), industrial emissions, and vehicular exhaust. In the atmosphere, they undergo chemical reactions with oxygen and water vapor to form sulphuric acid (H₂SO₄) and nitric acid (HNO₃), which dissolve in rainwater to produce acid rain with a pH less than 5.6. Acid rain harms ecosystems, damages buildings and structures, and poses risks to human health. Reducing emissions through cleaner fuels and pollution control technologies is essential to mitigate acid rain.

Important one-liners for upcoming exams:
☛ pH of acid rain → less than 5.6
☛ Main acids formed in acid rain → Sulphuric acid and nitric acid
☛ Primary gases responsible for acid rain → Sulphur dioxide and nitrogen oxides
☛ Effect of acid rain → Damages soil, water bodies, crops, and buildings
☛ Mitigation measure for acid rain → Use of clean fuels and emission control
question_hi: अम्लीय वर्षा मुख्य रूप से वायुमंडल में किन दो गैसों की उपस्थिति के कारण होती है? (RRB NTPC (UG) CBT-I (21/08/2025) Shift 2)

कार्बन डाइऑक्साइड और कार्बन मोनोऑक्साइड
नाइट्रोजन और मीथेन
सल्फर डाइऑक्साइड और नाइट्रोजन ऑक्साइड
solution_hi:
Solution: सही उत्तर है सल्फर डाइऑक्साइड और नाइट्रोजन ऑक्साइड

Explanation:
अम्लीय वर्षा वायुमंडल में सल्फर डाइऑक्साइड (SO₂) और नाइट्रोजन ऑक्साइड (NOₓ) की उपस्थिति के कारण होती है। ये गैसें मुख्यतः जीवाश्म ईंधनों (कोयला, पेट्रोलियम) के दहन, औद्योगिक उत्सर्जन और वाहनों से निकलने वाले धुएं से उत्पन्न होती हैं। वायुमंडल में ये गैसें ऑक्सीजन और जलवाष्प के साथ रासायनिक अभिक्रिया करके सल्फ्यूरिक अम्ल (H₂SO₄) और नाइट्रिक अम्ल (HNO₃) बनाती हैं, जो बारिश के पानी में घुलकर अम्लीय वर्षा का रूप लेती हैं। इसका pH मान 5.6 से कम होता है, जो पारिस्थितिकी तंत्र, भवनों और मानव स्वास्थ्य के लिए हानिकारक है। अम्लीय वर्षा के प्रभावों को कम करने के लिए उत्सर्जन नियंत्रण और स्वच्छ ईंधनों का उपयोग आवश्यक है।

question: Which physical feature acts as a barrier to the southwest monsoon winds, causing heavy rainfall on one side and dry conditions on the other? (RRB NTPC (UG) CBT-I (21/08/2025) Shift 2)
options: Aravalli Range
Western Ghats
Vindhya Range
Satpura Range
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Western Ghats

Explanation:
The Western Ghats act as a major orographic barrier for the southwest monsoon winds coming from the Arabian Sea. As the moisture-laden winds hit the Western Ghats, they are forced to rise. This upward movement causes cooling and condensation, resulting in heavy rainfall on the windward (western) side. In contrast, the leeward (eastern) side falls in the rain shadow zone, receiving significantly less rainfall, leading to dry conditions in the Deccan Plateau. The Western Ghats run parallel to the western coast of India and are a continuous mountain range. Other options like Aravalli, Vindhya, and Satpura ranges do not significantly obstruct the monsoon winds as they are either lower in altitude or aligned differently. The phenomenon is known as orographic precipitation.

☛ Other name of Western Ghats → Sahyadri
☛ Rain shadow region in Western Ghats → Eastern side (Deccan)
☛ Reason for heavy rainfall in Mumbai → Western Ghats
☛ States covered by Western Ghats → Gujarat to Tamil Nadu
question_hi: कौन सी भौतिक विशेषता दक्षिण-पश्चिम मानसून हवाओं के लिए एक बाधा के रूप में कार्य करती है, जिससे एक तरफ भारी वर्षा होती है और दूसरी तरफ शुष्क स्थिति होती है? (RRB NTPC (UG) CBT-I (21/08/2025) Shift 2)

पश्चिमी घाट
विंध्य रेंज
सतपुड़ा रेंज

Explanation:
दक्षिण-पश्चिम मानसून हवाएं अरब सागर से नमी लेकर भारत के पश्चिमी तट पर पहुंचती हैं। पश्चिमी घाट (Western Ghats) एक ऊंची पर्वत श्रृंखला है जो तट के समानांतर चलती है। यह मानसूनी हवाओं के लिए एक बाधा का काम करती है, जिससे हवाओं को ऊपर उठने के लिए मजबूर होना पड़ता है। ऊपर उठने पर ठंडी होकर संघनन होता है, जिससे पश्चिमी घाट के पश्चिमी ढलानों पर भारी वर्षा होती है, जबकि पूर्वी ढलान (दक्कन के पठार) पर वर्षा छाया क्षेत्र बनता है, जिससे शुष्क स्थिति रहती है। इस घटना को ऑग्रैफिक वर्षा कहते हैं। पश्चिमी घाट की तुलना में अन्य पर्वत श्रृंखलाएं (अरावली, विंध्य, सतपुड़ा) मानसून पर इतना प्रभाव नहीं डालतीं।

question: Which of the following industries was operational in India at the time of independence? (RRB NTPC (UG) CBT-I (21/08/2025) Shift 2)
options: Aerospace industry
Electronics industry
Iron and steel industry
Automobile industry
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Iron and steel industry

Explanation:
At the time of independence, the iron and steel industry was already operational in India. The Tata Iron and Steel Company (TISCO), established by Jamsetji Tata in 1907, was Asia's first integrated steel plant and a major industrial unit under British rule. Other options like aerospace, electronics, and automobile industries developed after independence. India's first iron and steel plant began production in 1912. This industry served as the backbone of Indian industrialization at independence.

question: The Western Ghats and the Eastern Ghats mark the western and the eastern edges of which plateau? (RRB NTPC (UG) CBT-I (21/08/2025) Shift 2)
options: Shillong Plateau
Chotanagpur Plateau
Malwa Plateau
Deccan Plateau
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Deccan Plateau

Explanation:
The Western Ghats and the Eastern Ghats mark the western and eastern edges of the Deccan Plateau in peninsular India. This triangular plateau is bounded by the Western Ghats on the west and the Eastern Ghats on the east. The Western Ghats are a continuous mountain range, while the Eastern Ghats are discontinuous. The Deccan Plateau is composed of basalt rocks formed by volcanic activity millions of years ago. Its average elevation is 600-900 meters and it slopes gently towards the east. The region is significant for agriculture, minerals, and biodiversity.

☛ What is the other name for Western Ghats? → Sahyadri
☛ Which is the highest peak of Eastern Ghats? → Mahendragiri
☛ What is the average elevation of Deccan Plateau? → 600-900 meters
☛ Which rivers flow over the Deccan Plateau? → Godavari, Krishna, Kaveri

question: The Atomic Energy Establishment, established at Trombay in 1954, was later renamed as:  (RRB NTPC (UG) CBT-I (21/08/2025) Shift 2)
options: Indira Gandhi Atomic Centre
Bhabha Atomic Research Centre
Indian Institute of Nuclear Science
Nehru Institute of Atomic Energy
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Bhabha Atomic Research Centre

Explanation:
The Atomic Energy Establishment, set up at Trombay (Mumbai) in 1954, was renamed as the Bhabha Atomic Research Centre (BARC) on 12 January 1967 in memory of Dr. Homi J. Bhabha, the father of India's nuclear programme and the first director of the institute. BARC is India's premier nuclear research facility, focusing on nuclear energy, reactor design, fuel cycle, radiation safety, and isotope production. It operates under the Department of Atomic Energy (DAE).

question: In dry areas, water from underground comes up through the soil by capillary action and dries quickly, leaving salts behind. These salts form a hard layer called:  (RRB NTPC (UG) CBT-I (21/08/2025) Shift 3)
options: hardpans
pedalfer
laterite
granite
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is hardpans

Explanation:
In dry regions, groundwater rises to the surface through capillary action and evaporates, leaving behind dissolved salts. Over time, these salts accumulate and form a hard, impermeable layer in the soil, known as hardpans. This layer restricts water drainage and root growth, making the soil less fertile. Hardpans are primarily composed of calcium carbonate, silica, or gypsum. They are a common feature in arid and semi-arid regions. In contrast, pedalfer refers to iron- and aluminum-rich soils found in humid regions, laterite is a tropical soil rich in iron and aluminum, and granite is an igneous rock. Understanding hardpans is important for soil management in dry areas.

Important one-liners for upcoming exams:

☛ Main components of hardpans? → Calcium carbonate, silica, gypsum
☛ What is pedalfer? → Acidic soil of humid regions
☛ Where is laterite soil found? → Tropical regions
☛ What type of rock is granite? → Igneous rock

question: Which of the following DOES NOT produce Greenhouse gases?  (RRB NTPC (UG) CBT-I (21/08/2025) Shift 3)

question: Which of the following was a major criticism of the Green Revolution in India? (RRB NTPC (UG) CBT-I (21/08/2025) Shift 3)
options: It reduced agricultural output
It discouraged use of technology.
It promoted organic farming.
It led to regional and crop imbalances.
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is It led to regional and crop imbalances.

Explanation:
The Green Revolution in India (1960s) introduced high-yielding variety (HYV) seeds, chemical fertilizers, and pesticides, boosting wheat and rice production. However, a major criticism was that it exacerbated regional disparities. States like Punjab, Haryana, and Western Uttar Pradesh with assured irrigation benefited disproportionately, while rain-fed and dry regions lagged behind. This led to crop imbalances as focus shifted to wheat and rice, neglecting pulses, oilseeds, and coarse grains. Small and marginal farmers, lacking access to capital and technology, were marginalized, worsening income inequality. Environmental degradation, groundwater depletion, and soil fertility loss were also significant criticisms. Thus, the Green Revolution's uneven regional impact and monocropping caused structural imbalances in Indian agriculture.

☛ Biggest negative impact of Green Revolution → Regional and crop imbalances

इसने प्रौद्योगिकी के उपयोग को हतोत्साहित किया।
इसने जैविक खेती को बढ़ावा दिया।
इससे क्षेत्रीय और फसल असंतुलन हुआ।
solution_hi:
Solution: सही उत्तर है इससे क्षेत्रीय और फसल असंतुलन हुआ।

Explanation:
हरित क्रांति (1960 के दशक) में उच्च उपज देने वाली किस्मों (HYV), रासायनिक उर्वरकों और कीटनाशकों के उपयोग ने गेहूं और चावल के उत्पादन को बढ़ाया। लेकिन इसकी प्रमुख आलोचना यह थी कि इसने क्षेत्रीय असमानताएं बढ़ाईं। पंजाब, हरियाणा, उत्तर प्रदेश जैसे सिंचित क्षेत्रों को लाभ मिला, जबकि सूखाग्रस्त क्षेत्र पीछे रह गए। इससे केवल गेहूं और चावल पर ध्यान केंद्रित हुआ, अन्य फसलों (दलहन, तिलहन) की उपेक्षा हुई, जिससे फसल असंतुलन पैदा हुआ। भूमिहीन गरीब किसानों और छोटे किसानों को प्रौद्योगिकी तक पहुंच नहीं होने के कारण आय में असमानता बढ़ी। इसके अलावा, पर्यावरणीय क्षति और मिट्टी की उर्वरता में गिरावट भी आलोचना के विषय रहे।

question: The Government conducted a crocodile census in the Vishwamitri River to estimate the population of mugger crocodiles. In which state is the Vishwamitri River located? (RRB NTPC (UG) CBT-I (21/08/2025) Shift 3)

Madhya Pradesh
Rajasthan
solution:

Explanation:
The Vishwamitri River is located in the state of Gujarat, flowing through the city of Vadodara. This river is known for its population of mugger crocodiles (Crocodylus palustris). The government conducted a crocodile census to estimate the population of these protected reptiles and plan conservation efforts. The Vishwamitri River is one of the major rivers of Gujarat and supports a suitable ecosystem for mugger crocodiles. It eventually empties into the Gulf of Khambhat. Gujarat state is actively involved in wildlife conservation, including periodic censuses.

question: Why is wheat grown in the north-western plains of India? (RRB NTPC (UG) CBT-I (22/08/2025) Shift 1)
options: Because it lies close to the coastal water bodies
Because it receives heavy rainfall during the monsoon
Because the region has fertile alluvial soil and cool winters
Because the region has red soil with limited annual rainfall
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Because the region has fertile alluvial soil and cool winters.

Explanation:
The north-western plains of India, particularly Punjab, Haryana, and western Uttar Pradesh, are ideal for wheat cultivation. The alluvial soil here, deposited by rivers, is highly fertile. Wheat is a rabi crop that requires cool temperatures; the region experiences cool winters, which are favorable for its growth. The area depends on irrigation as monsoon rainfall is limited, but canals and tube wells provide adequate water. Wheat needs cool weather for germination and warm weather for ripening, which the climate here offers. Thus, the combination of fertile alluvial soil and cool winters makes this region highly suitable for wheat farming, contributing to India's major wheat production.

☛ Major source of irrigation in north-western plains? → Canals and tube wells

Explanation:
भारत के उत्तर-पश्चिमी मैदान, विशेषकर पंजाब, हरियाणा और पश्चिमी उत्तर प्रदेश, गेहूं की खेती के लिए आदर्श हैं। यहाँ की जलोढ़ मिट्टी नदियों द्वारा लाई गई तलछट से बनी है, जो अत्यधिक उपजाऊ होती है। गेहूं एक रबी फसल है, जिसे ठंडे तापमान की आवश्यकता होती है; उत्तर-पश्चिम में सर्दियाँ ठंडी होती हैं, जो इसके लिए अनुकूल हैं। यह क्षेत्र सिंचाई पर निर्भर है क्योंकि मानसून की वर्षा सीमित होती है, लेकिन नहरों और ट्यूबवेलों से पर्याप्त पानी मिलता है। गेहूं को अंकुरण के लिए ठंडे मौसम और पकने के लिए गर्म मौसम की आवश्यकता होती है, जो यहाँ की जलवायु प्रदान करती है। इस प्रकार, उपजाऊ मिट्टी और ठंडी सर्दियाँ मिलकर इस क्षेत्र को गेहूं की खेती के लिए सबसे उपयुक्त बनाती हैं।

question: Which mode of transport is most suitable for transporting heavy and bulky goods over long distances? (RRB NTPC (UG) CBT-I (22/08/2025) Shift 1)

question: Littoral forests are most associated with which kind of ecosystem? (RRB NTPC (UG) CBT-I (22/08/2025) Shift 1)
options: Wetland ecosystem
Tundra ecosystem
Grassland ecosystem
Desert ecosystem
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Wetland ecosystem

Explanation:
Littoral forests are primarily found along river deltas, estuaries, and coastal areas where waterlogging conditions prevail. These forests are a part of the wetland ecosystem because the soil remains moist and the water table is high. They include mangroves, saltwater marshes, and coastal vegetation that can tolerate saline water and tidal influence. The wetland ecosystem is a transition zone between aquatic and terrestrial environments, hosting unique flora and fauna adapted to such conditions. Littoral forests are a classic example of this ecosystem, providing critical habitat and protecting coastlines from erosion.

☛ What characterizes a wetland ecosystem? → Transition between water and land

question: What is the primary cause of southwest monsoon in India? (RRB NTPC (UG) CBT-I (22/08/2025) Shift 1)
options: Tidal effects
Differential heating of land and sea
Westerly winds from the Atlantic
Local winds from the desert
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Differential heating of land and sea

Explanation:
The primary cause of the southwest monsoon in India is the differential heating of land and sea. During summer, the Indian subcontinent heats up rapidly while the Indian Ocean remains relatively cooler. This temperature difference creates a low-pressure area over land and a high-pressure area over the sea. The pressure gradient forces moisture-laden winds from the sea towards the land. When these winds encounter obstacles like the Western Ghats, they cause orographic rainfall. The monsoon is also influenced by the northward shift of the jet stream and the movement of the ITCZ. The monsoon typically arrives in Kerala by early June and covers the entire country by July.

question: Which of the following is responsible for causing convectional rainfall? (RRB NTPC (UG) CBT-I (22/08/2025) Shift 1)
options: Cyclonic movements
Intense surface heating causing air to rise
Mountains forcing air to rise
Cold and warm air masses meeting
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Intense surface heating causing air to rise.

Explanation:
Convectional rainfall occurs when the sun's rays intensely heat the Earth's surface, causing the air in contact with it to also heat up, become lighter, and rise. This rising air cools at higher altitudes, condenses to form cumulus clouds, and results in heavy rainfall. This type of rainfall is typical in equatorial regions and tropical areas during summer. It is usually heavy, short-lived, and accompanied by thunder and lightning. The intense heating creates strong updrafts, leading to vertical cloud development and precipitation.

question: Which type of rural settlement is most common in the northeastern states and Northern Plains of India? (RRB NTPC (UG) CBT-I (22/08/2025) Shift 3)
options: Dispersed
Semi-clustered
Hamleted
Clustered
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Clustered

Explanation:
In the northeastern states and the Northern Plains of India, clustered settlements are most common. These settlements are compactly grouped in a concentrated area, with houses adjoining each other. This type of settlement arises due to security, social ties, and shared resources. In the Northern Plains, fertile land and water availability lead to nucleated villages. In the northeastern states, limited flat land in hilly regions also promotes clustered settlements. These settlements are often located along riverbanks or roads. Dispersed settlements are found in hilly and arid regions, while semi-clustered and hamleted settlements are less common.

question_hi: भारत के पूर्वोत्तर राज्यों और उत्तरी मैदानों में किस प्रकार की ग्रामीण बस्ती सबसे आम है? (RRB NTPC (UG) CBT-I (22/08/2025) Shift 3)

अर्ध-गुच्छित
पुरवा
गुच्छित
solution_hi:
Solution: सही उत्तर है गुच्छित

Explanation:
भारत के पूर्वोत्तर राज्यों और उत्तरी मैदानों में गुच्छित बस्तियाँ सबसे आम हैं। ये बस्तियाँ एक सघन क्षेत्र में समूहित होती हैं, जहाँ घर एक-दूसरे से सटे होते हैं। इस प्रकार की बस्ती का कारण सुरक्षा, सामाजिक संबंध और संसाधनों का साझा उपयोग है। उत्तरी मैदानों में उपजाऊ भूमि और जल की उपलब्धता के कारण गाँव एक स्थान पर केन्द्रित होते हैं। पूर्वोत्तर राज्यों में पहाड़ी क्षेत्रों में सीमित समतल भूमि भी गुच्छित बस्तियों को बढ़ावा देती है। ये बस्तियाँ प्रायः नदी के किनारे या सड़क मार्ग पर स्थित होती हैं। प्रकीर्ण बस्तियाँ पहाड़ी और शुष्क क्षेत्रों में मिलती हैं, जबकि अर्ध-गुच्छित और पुरवा बस्तियाँ कम आम हैं।
